title: POC Weekly Sync - SDK tool/function calls + structured output
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint covering SDK integration for function/tool calls and structured output. Reviewed recent test results, discussed a parsing issue with structured JSON output, tuned batching/timeout settings, and agreed on next steps: updated benchmark run, security doc share, and a canary for dedicated routing. Action owners and due dates recorded.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Park: ok uh thanks everyone for joining  gonna kick us off. quick agenda, 1) run results 2) integration questions on SDK tool calls 3) structured output parsing and 4) next steps. leah you good to start with the results?
[00:18] Leah Marshall: yeah thanks Alex. we ran the latest set of 5k sessions overnight, focusing on product Q&A flow. overall precision looks up about three percent, response time median around 310 ms but tails at like 1.2s some requests. we also saw a few malformed JSON blobs when we turned on the structured output flag.
[00:40] Omar Ruiz: the malformed ones are when followups call the tool, right? it seems like the SDK's function call wrapper sometimes inserts an extra newline and our parser chokes.
[00:55] Jordan Kim: mmh, from our side that's a known quirk when streaming + function-calls is enabled, the stream boundary can split tokens and downstream lib parsers might not reassemble. there are two approaches: buffer until end-of-response or use the SDK helper .on('functionCall') hook that emits well-formed objects.
[01:17] Priya Desai: buffering adds like 200ms to latency on median, which is... not great. our product team cares about sub-400ms median.
[01:28] Samira Vale: Right. one thing to try is a small reassembly layer client-side: when you get a partial payload, keep concatenating until the closing brace, then attempt parse. that keeps most streaming benefits. we can share a snippet.
[01:44] Ben Carter: also want to flag that in our infra some requests go to a dedicated pool and others to hosted; we saw slightly different quantization variants in responses, wonder if that could change tokens.
[01:58] Alex Park: good note Ben  that ties to routing. Jordan can you confirm if the POC config is hitting the same model variant across both pools?
[02:10] Jordan Kim: currently the routing policy is region-first then cost-tier fallback. for the POC we pinned to the redwood-open-7b-v2 but there was a small roll earlier that created a v2q quantized copy; some requests went to that when capacity was low. behaviorally it's equivalent but you can get tiny tokenization diffs that break strict JSON equality.
[02:36] Leah Marshall: that explains it. our team had strict JSON compare checks in the validation harness. we can relax to whitespace-insensitive parse but prefer deterministic output.
[02:47] Omar Ruiz: question about the SDK usage  is there a recommended pattern for tool vs function calls? we have a set of internal tools (search, inventory-check, price-suggester) and want to map them to Redwood's tool call surface.
[03:03] Jordan Kim: yes, two patterns. 1) Use the SDK 'tool' abstraction for idempotent read-only ops like search and inventory-check; it keeps retries safe. 2) Use 'function' calls for side-effectful endpoints like price-suggester if it writes or mutates state  the SDK includes metadata to indicate idempotency. we'll add docs with examples.
[03:25] Priya Desai: any sample code? our engineer Omar's implementing now and hit a serialization issue with nested arrays in the tool payloads.
[03:36] Samira Vale: we have a sample repo  redwood/examples/sdk-tool-patterns  I'll paste link in the recap. common pitfall: don't pass raw big binary blobs; stringify and base64 small files. nested arrays should be schema validated client-side and we recommend contract tests.
[03:53] Leah Marshall: on results, we also observed a subtle hallucination where tool call acknowledged success but returned stale inventory counts  likely our tool returned cached data. worth noting but not a Redwood issue.
[04:06] Omar Ruiz: ok moving on structured output tuning: we tried forcing the model to return strict JSON with system prompt but still saw occasional trailing commas and extra commentary like 'note: estimated' in the JSON string.
[04:22] Jordan Kim: yeah forcing strict JSON purely with prompts is brittle; we recommend the structured-output plugin in the SDK which enforces a schema and will try to repair minor deviations. it's not perfect but reduces parse errors significantly.
[04:36] Priya Desai: how do we enable the schema enforcement?
[04:40] Jordan Kim: in the SDK client options set structuredOutput: { schema: yourJsonSchema, repair: true, maxRepairAttempts: 2 }  the repair step runs a lightweight pass on the model to clean up common issues.
[04:56] Omar Ruiz: will repair increase token usage and cost?
[04:59] Jordan Kim: slightly, because repair may invoke a short follow-up generation; in practice we saw 5-8% more tokens on repaired calls but a 60% drop in failed parses, so overall fewer retries.
[05:15] Alex Park: sounds like a tradeoff. Leah/performance targets?
[05:20] Leah Marshall: target is error-rate under 1% for parsing and median latency sub-400ms. current parse fail is ~3.7% so repair seems promising.
[05:30] Priya Desai: also curious about batching config  Omar you experimented with batchSize 8 vs 16?
[05:37] Omar Ruiz: yes batch 8 median 320 ms, batch 16 median 390 ms but throughput higher; tails got worse for batch 16. for live product we lean batch 8 to keep the tails in-check.
[05:50] Samira Vale: you can use dynamic batching in Redwood Dedicated to adapt batch sizes based on current latency SLO, and we can propose policies for that.
[06:01] Ben Carter: can we get logs at token level for the failed parses? right now our logging strips some tokens for PII.
[06:10] Jordan Kim: we provide token-level tracing in the Console for debug sessions  it's gated behind additional retention and security settings. for POC we can enable ephemeral traces; they will redact based on your PII rules if you provide a regex config.
[06:28] Priya Desai: next the security ask  they want to see KMS integration and audit logs for the canary.
[06:36] Alex Park: yep we'll send the integration guide. Samira will include KMS options and example IAM policies.
[06:44] Samira Vale: noted. also for the Dedicated canary, recommend a 5% traffic slice for 48 hours, with automatic rollback on error-rate > 2.5%.
[06:56] Leah Marshall: timeline check  we'd like to go live internal beta by end of month, final rollout mid-April. is that feasible?
[07:04] Alex Park: feasible if we hit two things: 1) run the full 50k benchmark with structuredOutput repair enabled and 2) complete security review. we'll aim to deliver the benchmark by March 6 and security docs by March 5.
[07:18] Omar Ruiz: on benchmarks, what metrics should we collect? we track latency percentiles, token cost, parse-error rate, and throughput. anything else?
[07:27] Jordan Kim: add model drift / quality regressions using your eval prompts, and end-to-end success rate per intent. also capture allocation per pool to detect routing anomalies.
[07:38] Priya Desai: ok for action items, can we recap owners?
[07:42] Alex Park: sure. Samira will send code samples and KMS guide. Jordan will run a dedicated routing check and share logs. Leah/Omar will run the 50k benchmark with repair on. I'll send updated pricing for a 6-month reserved capacity trial.
[07:58] Leah Marshall: one more note  competitor eval, our infra team ran a quick throughput comparison with Bedrock and saw similar medians but Redwood had better tail latency, which is good.
[08:10] Alex Park: nice. any blockers?
[08:13] Omar Ruiz: blocker: our parser still fails on arrays with trailing comments, need the repair to handle that.
[08:20] Jordan Kim: we'll flag that to the engineering team, and if needed create a short token-level transformation that strips JS-style comments pre-parse.
[08:30] Priya Desai: thanks all  schedule next sync same time next week?
[08:33] Alex Park: yep same time. I'll follow up with calendar.
[08:36] (meeting ends)

Note: Transcript contains minor transcription errors (model names sometimes mangled e.g., 'redwood-open' heard as 'redwood-opan'), speaker turns simplified.
